mainTopic: The ages for a child's נדרים and הקדש, who matures first, and the status of the middle year
overview: This amud opens with the last line of the previous discussion: a young יבם completes the marriage when he grows up, and can then give a גט. A new משנה then sets three stages for a child's vows. Before a certain age, a child's vows and הקדש mean nothing. In a middle year, we check whether the child understands. After that year, the vows always count. A girl reaches each stage one year before a boy. The גמרא explains why every clause of the משנה is needed. A ברייתא then shows the משנה follows רבי, while רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds that boys mature first, and the גמרא gives each side's reason. Finally, the גמרא asks how to treat a child who shows signs of maturity during the middle year, for punishments. רב and רבי חנינא say it is like before the time, and רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי say it is like after the time. רב המנונא challenges the second view from the משנה, and the discussion of his proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: When he grows up, he completes the marriage and may give a divorce
steps.stepSummary: The previous discussion ends: when the young יבם grows up, he lives with her as a full husband and can then divorce her with a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he grows up, he will live with her as husband and wife, and he can then give a bill of divorce.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line of the previous discussion about a young boy who did יבום. The גמרא wraps it up with the practical outcome once he is grown.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What the young boy did was not enough to make her his full wife. Once he is an adult, his act of marriage completes the bond. After that, a regular גט is the way to end the marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: when he grows up, meaning when he becomes an adult
he will live with her as husband and wife, completing the marriage
a bill of divorce

phrases.english: When he grows up, he will live with her and give a bill of divorce.
phrases.notes: This finishes the earlier discussion about a young boy who did יבום with his brother's widow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion from the previous section of the daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Once grown, the boy completes the marriage and may then end it with a גט.

steps.title: A girl's vows: checked at eleven, binding at twelve
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that from age eleven and a day a girl's vows are checked. From twelve and a day they stand automatically. The checking applies throughout her twelfth year.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A girl who is eleven years and one day old has her vows checked. A girl who is twelve years and one day old has vows that stand. We check her vows during the whole twelfth year.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives the ages at which a girl's vows start to count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two stages here. From eleven and a day, her vow counts only if checking shows she understands it. From twelve and a day, her vow counts with no check needed. The checking period is the year in between.

keyTerms.meaning: our משנה, the text being studied
vows, meaning promises that make something forbidden or create an obligation
are checked, to see whether the child understands the vow
stand, meaning they take effect automatically
we check

steps.confusionAlert: "Twelve years and one day" is when checking stops and her vows count automatically. The checking itself happens during the year before that, starting at eleven and one day.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:

phrases.aramaic: בַּת אַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד —
phrases.english: A girl eleven years and one day old —
her vows are checked.

phrases.aramaic: בַּת שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד —
phrases.english: A girl twelve years and one day old —
her vows stand,
and we check during all of the twelfth year.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּת אַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד נְדָרֶיהָ נִבְדָּקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A girl's vows are checked from eleven and a day and stand automatically from twelve and a day.

steps.title: A boy's vows: checked at twelve, binding at thirteen
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives the same pattern for a boy, one year later. His vows are checked from twelve and a day and stand from thirteen and a day.
steps.simpleTranslation: A boy who is twelve years and one day old has his vows checked. A boy who is thirteen years and one day old has vows that stand. We check his vows during the whole thirteenth year.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה repeats the same rule for a boy, but each stage comes one year later than for a girl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The structure is the same: first a year of checking, then automatic validity. The only change is the age. This shows the משנה treats a girl as reaching each stage one year earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: a boy thirteen years old, the age when his vows count automatically
his vows
and one day, meaning he has fully passed that birthday

steps.whyThisMatters: These ages, twelve for a girl and thirteen for a boy, are the familiar ages of בת מצוה and בר מצוה.

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד —
phrases.english: A boy twelve years and one day old —
his vows are checked,

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן שְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד —
phrases.english: a boy thirteen years and one day old —
his vows stand,
and we check during all of the thirteenth year.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֶּן שְׁתֵּים עֶשְׂרֵה שָׁנָה וְיוֹם אֶחָד נְדָרָיו נִבְדָּקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the same rule for a boy, one year later.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A boy's vows are checked from twelve and a day and stand automatically from thirteen and a day.

steps.title: Before the checking age, vows mean nothing even if the child understands
steps.stepSummary: Before the checking year begins, a child's vow or הקדש has no effect. This is true even if the child says they know in Whose name they vowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Before this time, even if they said, "We know in Whose name we vowed" or "in Whose name we made it holy," their vow is not a vow and their הקדש is not הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains what happens to a child who is younger than the checking year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Below eleven for a girl and twelve for a boy, understanding does not help. Even if the child clearly says they understand, the vow and the הקדש do not take effect. Age alone decides here.

keyTerms.meaning: before this time, meaning before the checking year
in Whose name, meaning to Whom the vow was made (to ה׳)
a vow
making something holy, dedicating it to the Beis HaMikdash

phrases.english: Before this time,
phrases.notes: Before eleven and a day for a girl, and before twelve and a day for a boy.

phrases.english: even though they said:
"We know in Whose name we vowed,"
"in Whose name we made it holy" —
their vow is not a vow
and their הקדש is not הקדש.

steps.triggerLanguage: קוֹדֶם לַזְּמַן הַזֶּה אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what happens to a child younger than the checking ages given in steps 2 and 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Below the checking age, a child's vow or הקדש has no effect, even if the child claims to understand.

steps.title: After the full age, vows count even if the child says they don't understand
steps.stepSummary: After the full age, a vow or הקדש takes effect. This is true even if the person says they do not know in Whose name they vowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: After this time, even if they said, "We do not know in Whose name we vowed" or "in Whose name we made it holy," their vow is a vow and their הקדש is הקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes with the other side of the rule: once a child reaches the full age, the vow counts no matter what.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here too, age decides and not what the person claims. Above twelve and a day for a girl and thirteen and a day for a boy, saying "I didn't understand" does not cancel the vow. Only during the middle year does the child's understanding decide.

keyTerms.meaning: after this time, meaning after the checking year
even though
we made it holy, meaning we dedicated it

steps.whatToRemember: There are three stages. Too young: the vow never counts. The middle year: it counts only if checking shows the child understands. Full age (girl 12 and a day, boy 13 and a day): it always counts.

phrases.english: After this time,
even though they said:
"We do not know in Whose name we vowed,"
"in Whose name we made it holy" —
their vow is a vow
and their הקדש is הקדש.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאַחַר הַזְּמַן הַזֶּה אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror image of step 4, for those past the full age.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the full age, a vow or הקדש takes effect even if the person claims not to understand.

steps.title: Why say that vows stand at twelve and a day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to say that at twelve and a day her vows stand. It already said the checking starts at eleven and a day.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Since the משנה already taught that at eleven years and a day her vows are checked, why do I need it to say that at twelve years and a day her vows stand?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה with a question. It asks why the second clause, 'at twelve and a day her vows stand,' is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumes the second clause is obvious. Once she is an adult her vows count, so why spell it out? The גמרא is setting up an answer that will show the clause teaches something new.

keyTerms.meaning: why do I need it? (asking why a line is not extra)

phrases.english: GEMARA: But since it taught
"A girl eleven years and one day old,
her vows are checked",
"A girl twelve years and one day old,
her vows stand" — why do I need this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא begins analyzing the wording of the משנה quoted in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new point does the clause 'at twelve and a day her vows stand' teach?

steps.title: Without it, we might keep checking forever
steps.stepSummary: Without that clause, we might think a woman's vows always need checking. The משנה teaches that at twelve and a day they stand without any check.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought we check her vows forever. So the משנה teaches us that at twelve and a day they stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The clause stops us from thinking that checking never ends.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה had only said 'checking starts at eleven and a day,' we would not know when it stops. Maybe a woman's vows would always need testing. The clause sets an end point: from twelve and a day, no testing is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: it might enter your mind to say (a mistaken idea we might have had)
it teaches us (the clause is there to fix that mistake)
forever, always

phrases.english: It might enter your mind to say:
we check forever,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The clause sets an end to checking. From twelve and a day, her vows stand with no test.

steps.title: Why say we check through the whole twelfth year?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks about the third clause. If vows stand at twelve and a day, why add that we check all through the twelfth year?
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the משנה taught that at twelve years and a day her vows stand, why do I need 'we check throughout the twelfth year'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a second question, this time about the third clause of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Checking starts at eleven and a day, and vows stand from twelve and a day. So it seems obvious that the year in between is the checking year. The גמרא asks what the extra words add.

keyTerms.meaning: we check during the entire twelfth year (between eleven and twelve)

steps.confusionAlert: 'The twelfth year' means the year between her eleventh and twelfth birthdays, not the year after she turns twelve.

phrases.english: And since it taught
"A girl twelve years and one day old,
her vows stand",
why do I need "we check throughout the twelfth year"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of question as step 6, now aimed at the third clause.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the clause 'we check throughout the twelfth year' add?

steps.title: Without it, we might stop after thirty days
steps.stepSummary: There is a rule that thirty days into a year count as a full year. Without this clause, we might stop checking after thirty days if she did not understand her vows. The משנה teaches that we keep checking all year.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: since the Master said thirty days in a year count as a year, if we checked her for thirty days and she did not understand how to vow, we should not check her any more. So the משנה teaches us to check all year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second question. The clause makes sure we keep checking her the whole year, even if early tests fail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The known rule that 'thirty days in a year count as a year' might suggest that thirty days of checking covers the whole year. Then a girl who failed in those thirty days would be treated as a child until twelve. The clause teaches that she can be tested again at any point that year, because her understanding may grow.

keyTerms.meaning: thirty days in a year count as a year
to say a vow clearly, understanding what it means
no more, not again

phrases.english: It might enter your mind to say:
since the Master said
"thirty days in a year count as a year",
where we checked her for thirty days
and she did not know how to vow clearly,
I might say: we should not check her again,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא: הוֹאִיל וְאָמַר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The clause stops us from ending the checks after thirty days. We keep checking her throughout the year.

steps.title: Then why mention eleven and a day at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה could have taught only the last two clauses. Then the first clause, 'at eleven and a day her vows are checked,' seems extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the משנה teach just these two clauses: 'At twelve years and a day her vows stand, and we check throughout the twelfth year.' Why do I need 'at eleven and a day her vows are checked'?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns things around and challenges the first clause. It claims the other two clauses already tell us everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we know that vows stand from twelve and a day, and that checking covers the whole twelfth year, then we already know checking starts at eleven and a day. So the first clause looks repeated. The גמרא sets up an answer showing it adds something.

keyTerms.meaning: let it teach (suggesting a shorter wording)
two clauses

phrases.english: Let it teach just these two clauses:
"A girl twelve years and one day old,
her vows stand,
and we check throughout the twelfth year."
"A girl eleven and one day old,
her vows are checked" — why do I need this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending the second and third clauses, the גמרא now argues the first clause is extra.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first clause of the משנה: 'at eleven and a day her vows are checked.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The last two clauses together already show that checking runs from eleven and a day until twelve and a day, so the first clause adds nothing.

steps.title: Even a very sharp girl is not checked before eleven
steps.stepSummary: Without the first clause, we might think a very bright girl could be checked earlier, during her eleventh year. The משנה teaches that checking never starts before eleven and a day.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed. You might have thought: an ordinary girl needs checking in her twelfth year and not in her eleventh, but a girl we see is extra sharp should be checked already in her eleventh year. So the משנה teaches us that she is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The first clause sets a fixed starting point that does not move earlier for a smart child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last two clauses only describe the normal case. Without the first clause, we might let a very bright girl be tested a year early. Saying 'eleven and a day' outright makes it a firm minimum age for everyone, matching step 4: before that, a vow has no effect at all.

keyTerms.meaning: it was needed
an ordinary, typical case
extra sharp, very bright

steps.whatToRemember: Every clause in the משנה has a job: eleven and a day is a firm starting point even for a bright child, the whole twelfth year is a checking period, and from twelve and a day vows stand with no check.

phrases.english: It was needed. It might enter your mind to say:
an ordinary girl needs checking in her twelfth year,
and in her eleventh year she does not need checking,
but where we see that she is extra sharp,
let us check her already in her eleventh year,
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is in the regular printed גמרא; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean she would be checked.

phrases.english: so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the clause is needed to block a mistaken idea (איצטריך).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A very sharp girl could be checked early, during her eleventh year.
steps.terutzMaskana: No girl is checked before eleven and a day, however bright she is.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All three clauses are needed. Eleven and a day is a fixed minimum age for checking, regardless of how sharp the child is.

steps.title: Why teach 'before this time' and 'after this time'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to say that vows are invalid before the checking period and valid after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the משנה need to say 'before this time' and 'after this time'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last two clauses of the משנה as extra. We already know when the checking period starts and ends, so what do these clauses add?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already gave the checking period (eleven and a day to twelve and a day for a girl). It seems obvious that before it the vows mean nothing, and after it they stand. So these clauses look unneeded.

keyTerms.meaning: Before this time (before the checking period)
After this time (after the checking period)

phrases.english: Before this time
and after this time,
why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: קוֹדֶם הַזְּמַן הַזֶּה וְאַחַר הַזְּמַן הַזֶּה, לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same pattern of asking why each clause of the משנה is needed, now aimed at the outer clauses.
steps.kashyaTarget: The clauses 'before this time' and 'after this time' in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once the checking period is defined, what happens before and after it seems obvious, so the clauses look extra.

steps.title: We don't rely on what the child says
steps.stepSummary: Without these clauses, we might think a child's own claim could change the result. The משנה teaches that it cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: this rule applies only when the children say nothing. But when they do say something (like a young child saying 'we know in Whose name we vowed'), we should rely on them. The משנה teaches us that we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that these clauses do teach something. Outside the checking period, we ignore what the child says about understanding the vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought a too-young child who says he understands could have a valid vow. We might also have thought an older child who says he doesn't understand could escape his vow. The משנה says 'before' and 'after' to show the age decides, not the child's words.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply (only in this case)
We should rely on them

steps.whatToRemember: Every clause of the משנה is needed: before the checking period the vows never count, and after it they always count, no matter what the child says.

phrases.english: It might enter your mind to say:
These words apply where
they do not say anything,
but where they do say something
phrases.notes: A younger child says 'we know in Whose name we vowed,' or an older child says 'we don't know.'

phrases.english: we should rely on them,
so it teaches us that we do not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the clause blocks a mistaken idea (צריכותא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the child says he understands (or doesn't), we would rely on his words.
steps.terutzMaskana: Outside the checking period, age alone decides. The child's words don't matter.

steps.title: רבי and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר disagree: who matures first?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the משנה follows רבי, but רבי שמעון בן אלעזר switches the ages of girls and boys.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: These are the words of רבי. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: what was said about a girl applies to a boy, and what was said about a boy applies to a girl.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that the משנה's ages (girls one year before boys) follow רבי. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, a girl is checked at eleven and a boy at twelve, because girls mature earlier. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר flips this: boys are checked at eleven and girls at twelve, because he holds boys mature earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: A young girl
A young boy
A teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two views. The משנה follows רבי: girls first. Only רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says boys first.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
These are the words of רבי.
רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says:
the things said about a girl
are said about a boy,
the things said about a boy
are said about a girl.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: whose opinion the משנה follows, and the opposing view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה follows רבי (girls mature first). רבי שמעון בן אלעזר reverses the ages (boys mature first).

steps.title: רבי's source: 'ויבן' means extra understanding
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that רבי learns from 'ויבן' that women were given extra בינה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: What is רבי's reason? As it is written: 'And ה׳ [God] built (ויבן) the rib.' This teaches that הקדוש ברוך הוא gave the woman more understanding than the man.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives the source for רבי's view that girls mature first. He reads the word 'ויבן' (built) as connected to 'בינה' (understanding).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The creation of the woman is described with 'ויבן', which sounds like 'בינה'. So רבי learns that women were given extra understanding. That is why a girl's vows are checked a year earlier than a boy's.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
And He built (here read as hinting to בינה)
Rib (side) of אדם
Extra understanding

steps.whyThisMatters: This דרשה is the basis for the משנה's ruling that a girl reaches the age of vows a year before a boy.

phrases.english: רב חסדא said:
What is the reason of רבי?
As it is written: 'And ה׳ [God] built the rib,'
phrases.notes: בראשית 2:22. Some versions add the word in square brackets.

phrases.english: this teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave
extra understanding to the woman
more than to the man.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind רבי's opinion from step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From 'ויבן' we learn that women were given extra בינה, so girls mature earlier.

steps.title: What does the other view do with this פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי שמעון בן אלעזר explains the word 'ויבן'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (רבי שמעון בן אלעזר), what does he learn from this פסוק?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי שמעון בן אלעזר does with the פסוק of 'ויבן'. This sets up the next step, which gives his explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק teaches that women have extra understanding, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר seems to go against it. So he must read the פסוק in a different way.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the opposing Sage): how does he use this source?

phrases.english: And the other one, what does he do with this verse?
phrases.notes: The other one is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. The rest of the question isn't spelled out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רבי's source to how the opposing Sage reads that same פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי שמעון בן אלעזר explains 'ויבן' if not as extra בינה.

steps.title: 'ויבן' means He braided חוה's hair
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר uses the פסוק for ריש לקיש's teaching: ה׳ braided חוה's hair and brought her to אדם.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs that פסוק for ריש לקיש's teaching. ריש לקיש said in the name of רבי שמעון בן מנסיא: 'And ה׳ [God] built the rib that He took from the man into a woman, and brought her to the man.' This teaches that הקדוש ברוך הוא braided חוה's hair and brought her to אדם הראשון. In the cities by the sea, they call braiding 'building.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר reads 'ויבן' as 'braided'. So the פסוק teaches about חוה's hair, not about understanding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the פסוק is used for the braiding lesson, it is not available to teach extra בינה. The proof that 'built' can mean 'braided' comes from how people spoke in coastal cities, where braiding was called 'building'.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (the פסוק is used for a different lesson)
He braided her (hair)
The cities by the sea (coastal towns)
'Building', the word used there for braiding

steps.whatToRemember: Both Sages use the same word 'ויבן'. רבי reads it as בינה (understanding), so girls mature first. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר reads it as braiding, so this פסוק gives no proof that girls mature first.

phrases.english: He needs that verse
for the teaching of ריש לקיש,
as ריש לקיש said
in the name of רבי שמעון בן מנסיא:
'And ה׳ [God] built the rib
which He took from the man into a woman
and brought her to the man.'

phrases.aramaic: — מְלַמֵּד שֶׁקִּלְּעָהּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְחַוָּה
phrases.english: This teaches that the Holy One, Blessed be He, braided the hair of חוה
and brought her to אדם הראשון,
for in the cities by the sea
they call braiding
'building.'
phrases.notes: That is why 'ויבן' (He built) can mean 'He braided.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר uses 'ויבן' to teach that ה׳ braided חוה's hair, based on coastal usage where braiding is called 'building'.

steps.title: What is the reasoning of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds that boys reach understanding earlier than girls.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, what is his reason?
steps.whatsHappening: We already know why רבי gives girls the earlier age (the extra בינה from 'ויבן'). Now the גמרא asks for the reason of the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 showed that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר uses 'ויבן' for something else, so he has no פסוק for extra בינה in women. But that only shows why he does not agree with רבי. The גמרא still needs a positive reason why he gives boys the earlier age.

keyTerms.meaning: What is his reason?

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר מַאי טַעְמֵיהּ?
phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar, what is his reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר מַאי טַעְמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining how רבי שמעון בן אלעזר reads 'ויבן', the גמרא asks for his own positive reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why would boys reach understanding before girls according to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר?

steps.title: Boys learn in their teacher's house, so cleverness comes first
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק explains that a boy is often in his teacher's house, so cleverness enters him earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר רב יצחק said: Since a boy is often found in his teacher's house, cleverness enters him first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. Boys spend time learning with a teacher, which sharpens their minds earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reason is based on life experience, not on a פסוק. Learning with a רבי builds sharp thinking, so a boy's vows can be taken seriously at an earlier age.

keyTerms.meaning: Cleverness, sharpness of mind
His teacher's house, where he learns
Often found, frequently present

steps.whatToRemember: רבי: girls first, because of extra בינה ('ויבן'). רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: boys first, because they learn in their teacher's house.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak said:
Since the boy is often found in his teacher's house,
cleverness enters him first.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Boys spend time with their teacher, so they become clever earlier.

steps.title: Does the in-between year count as before or after the time?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: if signs of maturity appear during the year when vows are checked, is that like before the time or like after the time?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: 'during the time', is it like 'before the time' or like 'after the time'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. The משנה has three periods, and the question is how to treat the middle one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the time, a child's vows do not count. After the time, they always count. During the time (the middle year), we check whether the child understands. The question is about a child who shows physical signs of maturity in this middle year.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked; the Sages were unsure
During the time: the middle year when vows are checked
Before the time
After the time

steps.confusionAlert: 'The time' here is the special year from the משנה when vows are checked (12th year for a girl, 13th for a boy). It is not a general word for age.

phrases.english: A question was asked of them:
'During the time' — is it like 'before the time',
phrases.notes: The case is a child who grows two hairs, the signs of maturity, during this middle year.

phrases.english: or like 'after the time'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after finishing the discussion of רבי and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How to treat signs of maturity that appear during the middle year.

steps.title: Which law is this question about? Not vows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what law the question matters for, and shows it cannot be about vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: For which law does this matter? If for vows, it is not like before the time and not like after the time.
steps.whatsHappening: Before answering, the גמרא checks what the question is really about. It rules out vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For vows, the משנה already tells us what to do in the middle year: we check the child's understanding. So hairs do not decide anything for vows, and the question cannot be about vows.

keyTerms.meaning: For which law does this matter?
Vows
It is similar to, it is like

phrases.english: For which law?
If for vows —
it is not like 'before the time',
and it is not like 'after the time'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the question of step 20 by ruling out vows as its subject.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical law depends on the question of step 20.

steps.title: The question is about punishments
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the question must be about punishments, and asks what the law is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, for punishments, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: Since it is not about vows, the גמרא says the question is about punishments. This line sets up the disagreement that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real question is: if a child in the middle year grew signs of maturity and then did an עבירה, is he punished like an adult? The גמרא now asks for the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Punishments for breaking a law of the תורה

phrases.english: Rather, for punishments, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ruling out vows in step 21, it names punishments as the real subject.

steps.title: A disagreement: before the time or after the time
steps.stepSummary: רב and רבי חנינא say the middle year is like before the time; רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי say it is like after the time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and רבי חנינא both say: during the time is like before the time. רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי both say: during the time is like after the time.
steps.whatsHappening: Two pairs of אמוראים disagree about the question. One pair says the child is treated as not yet grown; the other says the child is treated as grown.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If it is like before the time, the hairs do not count and the child is not punished. If it is like after the time, the hairs count as real signs of maturity and the child is punished like an adult.

keyTerms.meaning: Both of them

steps.whatToRemember: Middle year with signs of maturity, for punishments: רב and רבי חנינא say like before the time (not punished). רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי say like after the time (punished).

phrases.english: Rav and Rabbi Chanina, who both say:
'during the time' is like 'before the time',

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי דְּאָמְרִי תַרְוַויְיהוּ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, who both say:
'during the time' is like 'after the time'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answer to the question about punishments, as a disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב and רבי חנינא: the middle year is like before the time. רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי: the middle year is like after the time.

steps.title: A memory aid for who said what
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a פסוק to help remember which side each אמורא took.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק says: your memory aid is the פסוק "Now this was the custom in former times in Israel."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to give a memory trick, so we can remember which אמוראים said the middle year is like 'before the time.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וזאת is a feminine-sounding word, and רבי חנינא has a name ending like a feminine word. The word לפנים means 'before,' which reminds us that רבי חנינא (together with רב) holds the middle year is like 'before the time.' No new law is added here; it is only a tool for remembering.

keyTerms.meaning: Your memory aid; a sign to help you remember
In former times; 'before' (hinting at 'before the time')

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak says:
And your memory aid is:
"Now this was in former times in Israel."
phrases.notes: רות 4:7. The feminine-sounding וזאת points to רבי חנינא, and לפנים ('before') reminds you he says 'like before the time.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a memory aid for the מחלוקת listed in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק וזאת לפנים בישראל reminds us that רבי חנינא (with רב) holds the middle year is like before the time.

steps.title: A challenge from the end of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא argues that the end of the משנה implies the middle year counts like before the time, against רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא objects: the משנה says that after this time, even if they say 'We don't know in Whose name we vowed or consecrated,' their vow is a vow and their הקדש is הקדש. This implies that during the time, it is like before the time!
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא quotes the end of the משנה about children's vows and draws an inference that seems to go against רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says only 'after the time' do vows count even without understanding. So רב המנונא infers that 'during the time' does not get that full status, and is treated like 'before the time.' That fits רב and רבי חנינא, but challenges רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי, who say the middle year is like after the time.

keyTerms.meaning: After the time: past the age of adulthood
This implies; introduces an inference from what the text says

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna raises an objection:
After this time,
even though they said:
"We do not know in Whose name we vowed,"
"in Whose name we consecrated,"
their vow is a valid vow and their consecration is a valid consecration.
This implies that during the time,
it is like before the time!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the position of רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי from step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי, who say the middle year is like after the time.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה gives full adult status only 'after the time,' implying that 'during the time' is like before the time.

steps.title: רבא answers from the start of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא shows that the first part of the משנה implies the opposite, so the end cannot be a proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: read the first part. Before this time, even if they say 'We know in Whose name we vowed or consecrated,' their vow is not a vow and their הקדש is not הקדש. This implies that during the time, it is like after the time!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on רב המנונא by reading the first part of the same משנה, which seems to imply the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part says only 'before the time' are vows invalid even with understanding. That implies 'during the time' is like after the time. Since the two parts of the משנה point in opposite directions, רבא's point is that neither inference can serve as a proof.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a משנה
Before the time: under eleven years and a day for a girl, or twelve years and a day for a boy
Like after the time

steps.confusionAlert: Both inferences use the same word הא ('this implies'), but they come from different parts of the משנה and reach opposite results.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
Say the first part:
Before this time,
even though they said:
"We know in Whose name we vowed,"
"in Whose name we consecrated,"

phrases.aramaic: אֵין נִדְרֵיהֶם נֶדֶר וְאֵין הֶקְדֵּשָׁן הֶקְדֵּשׁ.
phrases.english: their vow is not a valid vow and their consecration is not a valid consecration.
This implies that during the time,
it is like after the time!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב המנונא's challenge by showing that the first part of the משנה implies the opposite.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the משנה entirely, without proving either side.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An inference from the end of the משנה is cancelled out by the opposite inference from its start.

steps.title: The גמרא says רבא misunderstood רב המנונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבא's answer, explaining that רבא wrongly thought רב המנונא was learning from an extra line in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is not so; רבא made a mistake. He thought רב המנונא was inferring from an extra line of the משנה, so he said: instead of inferring from the end, let him infer from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says רבא's answer does not work because he misread how רב המנונא was learning. This sets up the next move, where the גמרא will explain what רב המנונא really meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא assumed רב המנונא was learning from an unneeded line. If so, both lines are equally extra, and their inferences cancel each other out. The גמרא says this assumption was wrong, so רב המנונא's challenge still stands for now.

keyTerms.meaning: Made a mistake; erred
An extra or unneeded line in a משנה
Infers; learns something from careful reading
The last part of a משנה

phrases.english: But it is not so;
Rava made a mistake.
He thought
that Rav Hamnuna was inferring from an extra line of the משנה,
and so, instead of inferring from the last part,
let him infer from the first part.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's rejection in step 26, reviving רב המנונא's challenge.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבא's answer only; the explanation of רב המנונא's real reading comes next.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא wrongly assumed רב המנונא was inferring from an extra line, which could be cancelled by an opposite inference from the other part of the משנה.

steps.title: רב המנונא's proof comes from the plain words of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבא was wrong about רב המנונא's method. רב המנונא learned from the main wording of the משנה, not from an extra line. It begins by showing that 'after the time' must mean a boy who has two hairs.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so. רב המנונא learned his point from the משנה itself, like this: when the משנה says 'after the time,' what case does it mean? If the boy has not grown two hairs, he is still a minor. So it must mean a boy who has grown two hairs...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רבא's reading and begins rebuilding רב המנונא's proof step by step. This step is a setup, and the proof is finished on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא thought רב המנונא relied on an extra line in the משנה, so he could push back using the first part of the משנה. Now the גמרא says the proof comes from what 'after the time' must mean. A boy without two hairs is a קטן no matter how old he is, so 'after the time' must be talking about a boy who has two hairs. That point will be the base for the rest of the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is not so. This is the גמרא rejecting what was just said.
From the body of the משנה itself, meaning its plain main wording and not an extra line
What is the case? What situation are we talking about?
Two hairs, the physical sign of becoming an adult
A minor, not yet a halachic adult

steps.confusionAlert: Age alone does not make someone an adult. Even after the right age, a boy without two hairs is still a קטן. That is why 'after the time' must mean a boy who has two hairs.

phrases.english: But it is not so;

phrases.aramaic: רַב הַמְנוּנָא מִגּוּפָא דְּמַתְנִיתִין קָא דָיֵיק:
phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna infers from the mishna itself:
That case of "after the time": what are the circumstances?
If he has not developed two hairs,
phrases.notes: Literally 'brought two hairs,' meaning the hairs that show physical adulthood.

phrases.english: he is a minor.
Rather, is it not where he has developed two hairs,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא, רַב הַמְנוּנָא מִגּוּפָא דְּמַתְנִיתִין קָא דָיֵיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the rejection of רבא's answer from step 27 and starts re-explaining רב המנונא's challenge from step 25.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבא's understanding of how רב המנונא built his proof, which brings back רב המנונא's challenge against רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבא assumed the proof came from an extra line in the משנה. It actually comes from what the plain wording 'after the time' must mean: a boy who has two hairs.
